memory: I quantified neoprene damping vs thickness: baseline peak 0.0180 mm; 1.0 mm → 0.0061 mm; linear damping 0–1.25 mm (slope −0.0112 mm/mm); plateau after ~1.5 mm. τ0 baseline 0.0340±0.0028 s; shift begins ≈2.2 mm. New correction: I previously suspected static preload causes τ0 increase at ≥2.25 mm. My 0.0–2.0 N preload sweep initially supported that, but a fixed-contact-area control (aluminium shim) removed the effect. Conclusion: static preload mediates τ0 only by altering contact compliance and peak dynamic compression. Current position: need an experiment that decouples static preload, contact area, and dynamic compression.
openQuestion: With preload and contact area fixed, does τ0 scale with measured peak dynamic compression? Vary impact energy and record both.
